beats.cue_text: If you are in a position to make the payment, paying on time is better for you. This video is for people whose income has genuinely fallen, whose medical expenses have increased, who are trapped in credit card rotation, and who cannot manage their bills despite trying everything. Paying the required minimum on time can help keep the account from becoming overdue. The problem is that repeatedly paying only the minimum can keep the debt going for a long time. beats.cue_text: There is another important protection. Under RBI credit card rules, unpaid taxes, levies, and charges must not be capitalised to charge or compound interest on them. Does settlement mean all interest and penalties will be removed? In some cases, the bank may agree to waive part of the amount. But that is not an automatic right. scenes.chapter: Bank తో written గా · Hardship communication

beats.title: A clear hardship email
beats.te: Clear written communication పంపండి
beats.cue_text: Verify the grievance officer's or nodal officer's contact on the bank's official website. Send a hardship email there. You do not need fancy English. Explain your actual situation clearly. “My income has fallen.” “Medical expenses have made it difficult to manage the current payment.” “I am available to discuss repayment options.” “After essential expenses, this is the amount I can afford each month.” State the facts like this. Do not promise an amount you cannot afford. It is easy to say, “I will pay tomorrow,” just to end the call. But tomorrow, the same pressure returns, right? Honestly say, “I cannot commit to that amount. I need a workable option.” A reduced EMI. A repayment plan. Restructuring. Settlement. Ask in writing which options apply to your situation. You can also say that you prefer written communication. But requesting communication only by email does not mean the bank loses permission to make lawful calls. That request is a communication preference. The protections against harassment are a separate matter.

scenes.chapter: Recovery agents — rules & tricks · Your rights

beats.title: Calling hours — and limits
beats.te: Recovery agents contact చేయొచ్చు — కానీ limits లోనే
beats.cue_text: But insulting, threatening, or publicly humiliating you during recovery, or intruding on your family's privacy, is not allowed. Under RBI instructions, threatening or anonymous calls, inappropriate messages, and persistent harassment are prohibited. Calls to recover overdue dues must not be made before eight in the morning or after seven in the evening. Does that mean anything is acceptable between eight and seven? No. Following the time limit does not make harassment acceptable. “We will tell your neighbours.” “We will speak in front of everyone at your office.” “We will trouble your family.” If you face this kind of pressure, you do not have to accept it as a normal recovery process.

beats.title: Who is calling — for which bank?

beats.cue_text: Calmly ask, “What is your name? What is the agency's name? Which bank are you representing? Please send your authorisation details through an official email.” If they speak loudly, you do not have to raise your voice too. Your goal is not to win an argument. It is to document the situation and handle it through the correct channel. If necessary, say, “I have explained my hardship to the bank in writing. I will discuss payment options through the official channel. Please do not use threatening language.” Short. Clear. That is enough.

beats.cue_text: What if you get a WhatsApp message asking you to share your live location? First, pause. You do not have to share your location just because an unknown person asks. Officially verify their identity and bank authorisation. Never share an OTP, PIN, password, or card details. Asking for your location alone does not prove that someone is fake. But there is no need to give personal information without verification.

beats.cue_text: Do not assume every message is genuine. And do not dismiss every message as fake. That is a sensible approach.

Confirm through the bank app, official website, or verified customer care. Legal communication can also arrive electronically. So, do not assume it is fake just because it came through WhatsApp or email. Who sent it? Are there case details? Can you verify the court or the lawyer's information? Check these things. beats.cue_text: Now, what if someone actually comes to your house? First, stay calm. If you feel uncomfortable, you do not have to invite them inside. Ask for an ID card. Ask for the bank's authorisation letter. Verify which account the visit concerns. Speak only in a place where you feel safe. If needed, ask a trusted person to stay with you. “Sign right now.” “Give me cash.” “Give me your phone.” Do not immediately react to this kind of pressure. Read and understand any document. Sign only after getting advice if you need it. If there is force, a physical threat, or immediate danger, call the emergency number, one one two. Your safety comes first.

But keep a verified communication channel open. Check the bank's emails. Collect official letters. Silencing unknown calls may also make you miss job, hospital, or delivery calls, right? beats.cue_text: “If I do not answer the calls, will the file close after sixty days?” There is no such guarantee. The recovery agency may change. The bank's team may change. Calls may decrease and then increase again. But a change in the agency's assignment does not make the debt disappear. Your plan should not depend on silence. It should depend on a budget, written communication, evidence, and verified repayment options. Now, let us see what happens to the account from the due date onwards. Your statement has a due date.

scenes.chapter: Due date నుంచి NPA, write-off వరకు · The timeline

beats.title: How an unpaid card moves towards NPA
beats.te: Due date నుంచి NPA వరకు ఏం జరుగుతుంది
beats.cue_text: Your statement has a due date. By that date, you need to pay the full amount or the required minimum amount. If you do not pay the full bill, applicable finance charges may arise. If you do not fully pay the minimum amount either, the account becomes overdue. RBI rules say the credit card account must be past due for more than three days before late payment charges can be levied or the account reported as past due. But the days-past-due calculation starts from the original due date. So, do not treat those extra three days as a new due date. Do not plan to delay the payment. As the delay continues, collection follow-up may increase. Account restrictions may apply. Your credit report may be affected. Many people assume, “There will be no problem until ninety days.” That is incorrect. Even before NPA classification, there can be overdue reporting, charges, and recovery follow-up. Under RBI rules, if the minimum amount due shown in your statement is not fully paid within ninety days from the payment due date, the credit card account is treated as an NPA. What does NPA mean? In the bank's asset classification, the account has become non-performing. Bank accounting and provisioning rules apply.
beats.transition_owner: TeluguInserts layer (12-frame fade in/out over the dimmed stage)
actions: overdue cursor sweeps from the original due date
qualifications: NPA = minimum due not fully paid within 90 days from the due date; >3 days rule counted from original due date; not “no problem until 90 days”

beats.te: NPA అయింది కాబట్టి కట్టక్కర్లేదు — అది నిజం కాదు
beats.cue_text: But from your perspective, does NPA classification mean you no longer need to pay? No. Similarly, if the bank offers EMI conversion, look at the details before immediately saying yes.

beats.cue_text: No. Similarly, if the bank offers EMI conversion, look at the details before immediately saying yes. What is the monthly EMI, interest rate, and tenure? Is there a processing fee? What is the total repayment? Here is the most important question. Can you genuinely afford that EMI every month? Taking an unaffordable EMI just to escape credit card pressure can bring the same problem back in a new form next month. An affordable repayment plan may be useful. So, understand the offer before deciding. Now, let us talk about write-off.
beats.transition_owner: TeluguInserts layer (12-frame fade in/out over the dimmed stage)

beats.title: The books change. The claim remains.
beats.te: Write-off అంటే debt cancel అయినట్టు కాదు
beats.cue_text: Now, let us talk about write-off. Many people feel relieved when they hear that word. “Does that mean the bank has removed my debt?” That is where the confusion lies. A technical write-off is generally an accounting action. The treatment in the bank's books may change. But the claim against the borrower is not automatically waived. Recovery may continue. There is no universal rule that every card must be written off after one hundred and eighty days. The timing depends on the issuer's policy and the facts of the account. Waiting for write-off does not guarantee a large discount. When you are struggling, you can discuss workable options with the bank immediately. You do not necessarily have to wait for write-off to request a settlement. Now, let us discuss differences between banks. SBI Card, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, YES Bank, Kotak, RBL, and IDFC FIRST.

scenes.chapter: Settlement & Lok Adalat — safe గా · Settle safely

beats.cue_text: Okay. What does settlement actually mean? The bank agrees to accept part of its claimed dues and waive the remaining claim under agreed terms. It is a mutual agreement. Your request alone is not enough. The bank's approval is needed too. You can make a realistic proposal based on your income, hardship, and available funds. “This is the amount I can arrange at present.

beats.cue_text: “This is the amount I can arrange at present. I cannot commit to anything more. Please consider a full and final settlement,” you can ask. But borrowing again at very high interest to fund the settlement risks moving you from one problem into another. The settlement amount must be affordable. The payment deadline must be realistic. Here is an example. Suppose your outstanding amount is one lakh. A caller says, “Pay thirty thousand and we will close it.” That sounds like a relief, right? But do not make the payment immediately out of excitement. First, ask, “Can you send the official settlement letter?

beats.title: What a settlement letter must show
beats.cue_text: First, ask, “Can you send the official settlement letter? Can I verify this offer through the bank's customer care?” The offer's authenticity matters more than its amount. The settlement letter must clearly identify your name and account, the agreed amount, payment dates, and the schedule if there are instalments. If you pay the agreed amount fully and on time, how will the remaining dues be waived? Will there be any further claim? How will the account be reported? You need to understand all of this. Use communication from an official bank channel or an authorised settlement letter verified by the bank. Do not trust a WhatsApp screenshot alone. What if someone says, “Make a small payment first, and the letter will follow”? Confirm in writing whether that payment is part of the settlement or will be adjusted as a regular account payment. If money you pay believing it is a settlement is recorded as an ordinary part payment, that creates a misunderstanding, right? Get clarity before making the payment.

After completing payment, obtain written confirmation and the applicable No Dues or settlement completion certificate. If a court recovery case is already pending, confirm how those proceedings will be closed after settlement. A telephone assurance that “We will handle everything” is not enough.

beats.title: Nothing to fear — but read the terms

beats.cue_text: What about Lok Adalat? The name itself makes some people nervous: “Do I have to go to court? What will they ask me there?” A regular Lok Adalat offers an opportunity for the parties to reach a mutually agreed settlement. Eligible pending cases and pre-litigation disputes may also be brought there. They will explain the proposal. Understand the terms. Check whether they are affordable for you. Going there does not mean you have to accept any offer you receive. Consent matters in a regular Lok Adalat settlement. An award based on an agreed settlement is final and binding, like a civil court decree. There is no ordinary appeal. So, understand the amount, dates, and consequences clearly before signing.

scenes.chapter: Settled vs Closed, CIBIL rebuild · Rebuilding credit

beats.title: Two different statuses
beats.te: Settled, Closed — రెండూ వేరు
beats.cue_text: “Settled” generally indicates a payment below the full contractual dues, made with the lender's consent. “Closed” is a different status, associated with an account that has been fully repaid. Lenders may view a “Settled” status negatively. It can affect future loan or card approvals. Receiving a No Dues Certificate does not mean your credit report must show “Closed”. Settlement completion and credit reporting status are two different things.

beats.title: First, stabilise

beats.cue_text: Yes, you can. But there is no instant reset. First, stabilise your income. Make your monthly budget manageable. Build a small emergency fund. Just because you feel relieved that the debt has been cleared, you do not need to take new credit immediately. Later, if it is suitable for you, you can consider an FD-backed secured credit card.

Approval, deposit requirements, and limits depend on the issuer's policy. Making an FD does not guarantee card approval. And do not lock up all the savings you need for emergencies just to get a card. Once you get the card, use it only for small, planned expenses.

beats.cue_text: Today, you may feel afraid or confused. You may not know how to tell your family. But talk to a trusted person. It could be a family member you feel safe with, or a friend. You do not have to carry every detail alone. When you explain your situation, you do not have to begin by saying, “I have ruined everything.” “I am facing financial difficulty. These are my accounts. This is my current income. This is the plan I want to follow. I need support.” You can say that. It is not a weakness. It is a practical step towards facing the problem. Okay. beats.title: Everything so far — as one plan
beats.te: ఇప్పటి వరకు మాట్లాడిందంతా ఒక simple plan గా
beats.cue_text: Okay. Let us remember everything we have discussed as a simple eight-step plan. Step One. List all your accounts. Calculate your income, essential expenses, and the money available for repayment. Understand your agreement's terms and any set-off risk involving your salary account. Step Two. Explain your hardship through each issuer's official grievance channel. Ask for affordable repayment options in writing. Save complaint IDs and replies. Step Three. Organise recovery communication. Use spam controls. But make sure you do not miss verified bank emails, official letters, or genuine legal notices. Step Four. Review the cycle of covering old debt with new borrowing. Understand the benefits and costs of paying the minimum due. Do not make promises your budget cannot support. Step Five. If there are threats, humiliation, or abusive messages, save the evidence and complain. If necessary, escalate through the RBI complaint process. In immediate danger, call one one two. Step Six. Remember the difference between NPA, write-off, and settlement. Write-off does not cancel the debt. Discuss workable options instead of blindly waiting for a discount. Step Seven. If you settle, verify the official offer. Understand the amount, dates, waiver terms, and credit reporting status. Pay through an authorised channel and obtain receipts and confirmation of completion. Step Eight. Stabilise your income. Build emergency savings. Check your credit report. Then, if necessary, rebuild your credit profile with suitable secured credit and regular payments in full.
